title: UVM: Driver and Monitor
constraints: Write `stream_driver` (extends `uvm_driver #(stream_item)`) and `stream_monitor` (extends `uvm_monitor`, with a public `uvm_analysis_port #(stream_item) ap`). Both get `virtual stream_if` from `uvm_config_db` with field name `"vif"`.

**Driver:** keep `valid = 0` during reset (`rst = 1`). For each item, drive `data` with `valid = 1` on a clock edge and hold both stable until the byte transfers (a rising edge with `valid && ready`). Back-to-back transfers are allowed.
**Monitor:** on every rising edge with `valid && ready` (outside reset), write a **new** `stream_item` holding the transferred byte to `ap`. It must see every transfer exactly once.
The DUT applies random backpressure. Your driver and monitor are graded separately.
hints: Driver loop: `get_next_item`, drive with nonblocking assignments, `do @(posedge vif.clk); while (!vif.ready);`, drop valid, `item_done`.
Monitor: sample at `@(posedge vif.clk)`. The values you read there are the pre-edge values, which is exactly what the DUT saw.
A monitor that reuses a single item object corrupts every transaction already sent to subscribers: they all hold a handle to the same object.

examples.check: driver delivers every item in order
examples.title: driver
examples.expected: the DUT receives the same 300 bytes

examples.check: monitor reports each transfer exactly once
